data.name: Asaram
data.gender_notes: Asaram is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Asaram means 'calm' or 'free from sorrows'. In Hindu mythology, Asaram is a name of Lord Rama and is associated with strength, wisdom, and compassion. The name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'asrama', meaning 'hermitage' or 'place of retreat'. The name Asaram carries the meaning “Calm, Free from Sorrows” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Asaram usually hope their child will grow to embody calm, free from sorrows and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name rooted in the spiritual tradition of Hinduism, symbolizing inner peace and resilience.
data.etymology: Asaram belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Calm, Free from Sorrows.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Asaram total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Asaram holds great cultural significance in Hinduism. The name is associated with Lord Rama, one of the most revered deities in Hinduism. Rama's name itself implies the qualities of truthfulness, righteousness, and courage. By choosing the name Asaram, one is paying homage to these noble qualities and reminding themselves of the path of peace and calmness that leads to a fulfilled life.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Asaram lies in its meaning as a place of retreat or a state of peace and calmness. This resonates with the Hindu philosophy that encourages individuals to seek inner peace and enlightenment. The name reminds one to seek ashrama, or refuge, in the ultimate truth and to strive towards a life free from sorrows and inner peace. Thus, Asaram is not just a name but a reminder of the spiritual journey towards self-realization.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Asaram signifies the inner guru or the pure self within, guiding one through the maze of life towards the ultimate truth and inner peace. It represents the pursuit of self-realization and the path of righteousness.

historical_references.reference: Asaram Bapu was a prominent Hindu spiritual leader known for his teachings on nonviolence and self-reliance. He was born on August 17, 1941, in Gujarat, India. He rose to prominence in the late 1970s and 1980s and continues to be a significant figure in Indian spirituality today.

Asaram Bapu is also known for his involvement in various social and humanitarian causes. In the 1980s, he established the 'Gurukul Ashram' in Gujarat, which provides education and shelter to over 50,000 children. He has also been involved in various campaigns to promote environmental awareness and social harmony in India.

modern_usage.modern_context: Asaram Bapu is a well-known spiritual leader from India who has gained popularity through his teachings of yoga and spirituality. He has a large following on various platforms including YouTube where he has numerous videos of his sermons and teachings. On Twitter, he is an active user engaging with his followers and addressing their queries. However, Asaram has also been embroiled in several controversies which have given him negative publicity. These controversies include allegations of sexual misconduct and involvement in criminal activities. Despite these controversies, Asaram continues to have a significant following and remains a popular figure in the spheres of yoga and spirituality.
